handoff_policy.notes: Volatile artifacts are machine-managed or generated; handoffs record their existence, not their hash. Extra evidence outputs not declared in this contract are audit-only and must not invalidate a reviewed handoff.

principles: The previous step's formal artifact is the next step's input; chat history is not formal input.
workflow-state.json is an index, not a source of truth.
Artifacts that have not been approved must not be treated by downstream steps as approved input.
At the end of every step, show file paths, content summary, self-check results, pending approval items, and next-step inputs.
Missing/conflicting/stale inputs must block or be explicitly flagged; never fabricate.
Stage state can only advance atomically via scripts/workflow.py transition; Skills must not directly edit completed_steps/current_step.
Stage completion does not equal approval: you must request-review to freeze the current stage and end the turn; transition only after the user explicitly approves (approve).
Stage handoffs must generate a SHA-256 manifest; downstream entry points verify file hashes.
After the implementation stage, an independent read-only Verifier must produce machine-checkable evidence; only PASS may proceed to human acceptance.

Extending an existing system or modifying existing code requires actually reading the code location and recording exploration conclusions; third-party interfaces must record the provider, contract, sandbox, and test double; never assume from memory.

input_policy.principle: Read the small entry point first, then read by ID on demand; complete product/architecture baselines, ADRs, and complete specs are read only when necessary; never load everything into context by default.
read_order: 0. Resident: docs/product/BASELINE-BRIEF.md (when present; Stage 02 creates it if absent; about one page)
1. Stage 02: user-provided project materials and existing baseline records; Change stages: current proposal/specs/user-stories/tasks/design/baseline-impact/baseline-binding
2. Targeted: read only the FLOW/NODE/DO/RD/BR/ROLE/CAP/PAGE/API/IO/INTERFACE rows or sections matched by this Change
3. On demand: complete product/architecture baselines, ADRs, reference-research, complete specs; record the trigger reason

budget.note: Advisory guideline: when exceeded, narrow the scope or record in the handoff report why the extra reads are needed; never stuff the entire baseline into context. It is not a gate.

rules: Stage 02 is project-level discovery and may run before BASELINE-BRIEF exists; use the user goal as the source and create the brief in this stage. Later stages read the brief first and current Change artifacts next.
Read BASELINE-BRIEF and current Change artifacts first when present, then read by ID on demand; complete product/architecture files are not default inputs.
Architecture files are the output of stage 03; stages 05–10 read the corresponding sections only when the design domain matches, never in full by default.
ADRs are read only for decision conflicts/exceptions; complete specs are read only when the existing spec is insufficient.
Section 1 of the handoff report must list the files/sections actually read; on-demand files not read must not be claimed as reviewed.

lean: User-provided interviews, business/legacy materials, project goals, users, roles, constraints, pain points, and success criteria; do not scan unrelated locations.
Stage 02 contract and required template rows: process/STEP-ARTIFACT-CONTRACTS.json step 02; process/OUTPUT-TEMPLATE-MATRIX.csv Requirements business analysis rows.

docs/product/BASELINE-BRIEF.md (when present; Stage 02 creates or refreshes it).

on_demand: Complete existing docs/product/* only when a conflict or baseline-wide re-evaluation requires it; record the trigger and sections read.

docs/architecture/* and docs/adr/* only when existing approved architecture or decisions constrain a requirement.

output_policy.principle: Reference-style output: do not copy the full input text; baseline/spec/upstream artifacts are referenced by ID/path/section; each output carries only this stage's new decisions, contracts, or evidence.
rules: Summary files (BASELINE-BRIEF, requirements-analysis, baseline-audit-report, acceptance.md) contain only conclusions/deviations/evidence and do not repeat detailed tables.
design.md contains only this Change's decisions/contracts/implementation constraints/test mapping; baseline content is referenced by ID, not copied in full.
Evidence files (code-review, independent-verification, acceptance) reference JSON/log/report paths and do not restate all test output.
Tables retain only decision items/contract items/evidence items; fixed template fields are not expanded repeatedly.
output_policy.summary_budgets_note: Advisory line/char budgets: scripts/check-output-context.py reports over-budget files as warnings by default; --strict opts into enforcement.

stage_focus.02: requirements-analysis contains only goals/roles/process conclusions and deviations; details go in workflows/data-objects/rd-matrix/business-rules.
stage_focus.03: Each architecture file covers its own domain; technology-decisions contains only decisions/interviews; do not copy the complete product baseline.
stage_focus.05: proposal.md contains proposal-level initial design decisions (about one page); do not create design.md; interface/frontend/backend/test details are deferred to 07.
stage_focus.07: design.md references figma-audit/interface-catalog/test-cases/traceability; do not copy the full Figma spec or the entire baseline.
stage_focus.10: acceptance.md references the independent-verification report/JSON and test-cases; contains only sign-off conclusions and deviations.

rules: Each feature Change creates a baseline applicability/impact list in stage 05, recording each domain's baseline version, files/sections/IDs read, constraints, and reuse items; stages 06–07 review it and stage 10 completes the write-back decision during acceptance.

Local behavior/endpoints/pages/physical migrations/IO/tests stay in the Change; only changes to shared business rules, architecture boundaries, core domain models, shared contracts, or global quality gates trigger a baseline amendment.
Baseline changes require approval by the relevant owner and must be versioned; if they affect feature design or implementation, approve the baseline amendment before continuing affected work.
When conflicts are found during implementation, pause affected tasks and do not modify the frozen baseline directly; after approval, refresh the Change snapshot/design/tests.
At acceptance/archive time, write back only decisions that are approved, implemented, verified, and reused across features; feature-specific design stays in the archived Change.
After a baseline version change, in-flight Changes must undergo a NO_IMPACT / REBASE_REQUIRED review.
